content: International Nurses Day (IND) is observed globally every year on May 12. This day is dedicated to honoring and recognizing the invaluable contributions that nurses make to society. The International Council of Nurses (ICN) has been commemorating this day since 1965. In the United States, the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare had previously proposed that then-President Eisenhower declare a Nurses Day, but the proposal was not approved. In January 1974, it was decided to celebrate International Nurses Day on May 12, as this date marks the birth anniversary of Florence Nightingale, who is widely regarded as the founder of modern nursing. Each year, the ICN prepares and distributes the International Nurses' Day Kit, which includes educational and public information materials for nurses worldwide. However, Florence Nightingale is no longer universally seen as a role model in some parts of the world. For instance, the British public sector union UNISON has called for the observance of this day to be moved to another date. One suggestion has been May 21, the birthday of Elizabeth Fry (1780–1845), who founded the Institution of Nursing Sisters and is also known for her work with prisoners. Additionally, since 1998, May 8 has been designated as National Student Nurses Day in the United States, celebrated annually. Since 2003, National School Nurse Day has been observed on the Wednesday within National Nurses Week, which takes place from May 6 to May 12 each year. In the United Kingdom, a service is held annually on May 12 at Westminster Abbey in London. During this service, a symbolic lamp is taken from the Nurses' Chapel in the Abbey and passed from one nurse to another before being handed to the Dean, who places it on the High Altar. This act symbolizes the transfer of knowledge from one nurse to another. Additionally, at St. Margaret's Church in East Wellow, Hampshire, where Florence Nightingale is buried, a service is held on the Sunday following her birthday. In the United States and Canada, National Nursing Week is celebrated annually from May 9 to May 15. In the United States, this observance was officially established by President Richard Nixon in 1974.
